descriptionAdvanced.en: The Gran Chaco Liquid Separation Plant (Carlos Villegas) is a massive and strategically vital industrial facility located near the border city of Yacuiba in southern Bolivia. As one of the largest gas processing plants in South America, its primary function is to extract valuable liquid components—such as ethane, propane, and butane—from the natural gas stream before it is exported to Argentina and Brazil. This allows Bolivia to produce its own Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) for domestic consumption and export, as well as providing the raw materials for a future petrochemical industry. The plant represents a multi-billion dollar investment in the nation's energy sovereignty and has positioned Bolivia as a major regional player in the hydrocarbon value chain.

en: The plant has a processing capacity of over 32 million cubic meters of natural gas per day.
It is the third-largest liquid separation plant in Latin America.
The facility was inaugurated in 2015 and is operated by the state oil company YPFB.
It has made Bolivia self-sufficient in LPG and turned the country into a net exporter of the fuel.
